name: Inspect and certify treating iron
summary: Treating iron is the steel pipe, swivels, valves and fittings that carry fluid at up to 15,000 psi from the pumps to the wellhead, and uncertified or worn iron cannot go to location. A planner tracks each piece's certificate by serial number and arranges for due pieces to come home with fleet moves; yard staff wash them, technicians strip, inspect and measure wall thickness, rebuild valves, pressure test the pieces in a barricaded bay, and record, band and certify them. The work waits on fleet moves and batches, and mistyped serial numbers and missed wear are the main sources of error and risk.

baseline.org_archetype: A Canadian pressure pumping company with six to eight crewed frac fleets, about 16 cementing units and six coiled tubing crews, maintained from district shops in Alberta and northeast BC.
baseline.notes: Common practice of large WCSB pressure pumpers in 2019-2022: an ERP plant maintenance module for work orders, hour readings from engine controllers and the data van, paper or tablet checklists, spreadsheets and phone calls between shops and field crews.

trigger: A piece of treating iron reaches its certificate expiry or comes back from location damaged or leaking.
end_state: The piece is tested, recorded, banded and staged with a valid certificate, or condemned and a replacement ordered.

volume.seasonality: Steady through the year with iron rotated out as its certificate nears expiry; heavier in spring break-up and summer when parked fleets send whole iron trailers in for recertification before the next season.

evidence.note: Organisation file volume, checked against fleet size: a frac fleet carries roughly 300-500 pieces of treating iron, valves, swivels and fittings (manifold trailer, missile, ground iron and spares); with 7-8 fleets, about 17 cementing units and 9 coiled tubing units at 30-40 pieces each, the company holds about 4,000-5,000 pieces, which on a yearly certificate gives 350-450 a month, plus items pulled early for damage or valve rebuilds.

surge.cause: Spring break-up: parked fleets send their iron in for recertification before the next season

evidence.note: Break-up reduces field activity (src1) and road bans start with the spring thaw (src6). The multiplier is tier C.

Dispatch and crew scheduling board (scheduling module, whiteboards, spreadsheets)

steps.name: Pull the iron due list by serial number
steps.description: The maintenance planner filters the iron register (a spreadsheet or equipment list in the maintenance module) for pieces whose certificate expires in the next 30 to 60 days, grouped by fleet, and adds pieces crews have reported as damaged or leaking.

error.defect_description: A piece's serial is mistyped or missing from the register, so its expiry is missed.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of heavy equipment maintenance in WCSB pressure pumping companies.

steps.name: Arrange an iron swap with the fleet
steps.description: The planner emails the frac operations coordinator or district dispatcher the list of pieces to send home and arranges certified replacements to go out on the next pad move, so the fleet is never short of iron on location.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of heavy equipment maintenance in WCSB pressure pumping companies.

steps.name: Haul iron back to the base
steps.description: The due pieces come home on an iron trailer or float with the next equipment move, often a week or more after the swap is agreed, because iron moves only when the fleet moves between pads.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of heavy equipment maintenance in WCSB pressure pumping companies.

steps.name: Receive and log the iron
steps.description: A yard operator unloads the iron with a forklift, reads each serial number or band and ticks it off the due list, and sets aside unmarked or damaged pieces for the shop.

error.defect_description: A piece is logged under the wrong serial number.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of heavy equipment maintenance in WCSB pressure pumping companies.

steps.name: Clean and strip the iron
steps.description: The yard operator pressure washes sand, cement and fluid residue out of each piece, degreases threads and removes old paint bands so the surfaces can be inspected.

evidence.note: Cleaning and prep as the first recertification step (src7). Minutes tier C.

steps.name: Disassemble unions, swivels and valves
steps.description: A technician breaks out hammer unions, removes seals, takes swivel joints apart and opens plug and check valves so that bores, seal faces and threads can be seen.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of heavy equipment maintenance in WCSB pressure pumping companies.

steps.name: Inspect visually for wear and damage
steps.description: The pump technician checks threads, union wings, seal faces and bores for erosion, cracks, pitting and mismatched parts against the manufacturer's rejection criteria, and checks the part number and pressure rating stamped on each piece.

error.defect_description: Early erosion or a hairline crack is missed.

control.basis: Company iron integrity procedure based on manufacturer inspection criteria for high-pressure flow iron and hammer unions

evidence.note: Inspecting hammer unions for excessive wear (src4); visual inspection for defects (src7). Reject share tier C.

steps.name: Measure wall thickness
steps.description: The technician takes ultrasonic thickness readings at marked points on each piece, mostly at bends and in the flow path where erosion is worst, and compares them with the minimum wall table for the part number.

error.defect_description: A reading is taken at the wrong point or typed wrongly.

evidence.note: Non-destructive testing with meters (src7). Shares and minutes tier C.

steps.name: Send for magnetic particle inspection
steps.description: On a longer cycle, pieces go to a third-party NDT company that inspects threads and high-stress areas for cracks with magnetic particles and returns a report by serial number.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of heavy equipment maintenance in WCSB pressure pumping companies.

steps.name: Redress and rebuild
steps.description: The technician replaces seals and O-rings, rebuilds plug valves with new inserts and seal kits, and greases and reassembles unions and swivels.

error.defect_description: A seal is pinched or a valve is reassembled wrongly.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of heavy equipment maintenance in WCSB pressure pumping companies.

steps.name: Set up the test bay and clear the area
steps.description: Before each test batch the technician connects the pieces to the test pump inside the barricaded test bay, restrains the line, closes the bay doors and checks that nobody is inside the exclusion zone.

control.basis: Company pressure testing procedure: barricaded test bay, line restraint and exclusion zone during hydrostatic tests

evidence.note: Keep non-essential personnel clear and fasten high-pressure lines (src4). Minutes per piece tier C.

steps.name: Hydrostatic test
steps.description: Two technicians pump water into the pieces in stages up to the test pressure for the piece's rating, hold it for the set time while the chart recorder runs, and watch for pressure drop or leaks from outside the barrier.

evidence.note: Hydro-testing as a recertification step (src7); test pressure above working pressure but below component failure pressure (src4). Minutes and shares tier C.

steps.name: Record results by serial number
steps.description: The technician types each piece's serial number, thickness readings, test pressure, hold time and date into the iron register and scans the chart.

error.defect_description: A serial number or reading is mistyped.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of heavy equipment maintenance in WCSB pressure pumping companies.

steps.name: Review and sign the records
steps.description: The shop manager checks a batch of records against the charts and thickness tables, sends back pieces with missing or odd entries and signs the batch.

control.basis: Customer and insurer audits of treating iron certification records; company iron integrity procedure

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of heavy equipment maintenance in WCSB pressure pumping companies.

steps.name: Band, paint and issue the certificate
steps.description: The technician fits a coloured band for the certification period and paints the piece, and the planner issues the certificate and updates the expiry date in the register. Certified iron is staged on racks for the next fleet move.

evidence.note: Banding and painting after the hydro-test (src7). Minutes tier C.

steps.name: Decide on a borderline reading
steps.description: The equipment engineer compares the borderline thickness readings with the manufacturer's minimum wall and the piece's pressure rating, and either accepts it for a shorter period or condemns it.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of heavy equipment maintenance in WCSB pressure pumping companies.

steps.name: Condemn and cut the rejected piece
steps.description: The technician paints the rejected piece red, cuts or marks it so it cannot be used again, and records the reason in the iron register.

control.basis: Company iron integrity procedure: condemned iron is marked and removed from service

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of heavy equipment maintenance in WCSB pressure pumping companies.

steps.name: Requisition a replacement
steps.description: The planner raises a requisition for a replacement piece of the same part number and pressure rating and notes the fleet it must go to.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of heavy equipment maintenance in WCSB pressure pumping companies.

exceptions.name: Rejected on inspection or test
exceptions.description: Wear, a crack indication, wall loss or a structural failure on test condemns the piece and a replacement is ordered.

exceptions.name: Third-party crack inspection
exceptions.description: Pieces on their longer cycle go to an outside NDT company for magnetic particle inspection, adding about a week.

exceptions.name: Leak on test
exceptions.description: A seal or valve leaks on the hydrostatic test and the piece is rebuilt and retested.

exceptions.name: Borderline wall thickness
exceptions.description: The engineer decides whether a piece near minimum wall can stay in service.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from due list to certified iron staged for the next move
benchmarks.population: Treating iron recertification at a WCSB pressure pumper, 2019-2022

evidence.note: Author's estimate: iron comes home only with fleet moves (about a week) and is processed in batches; no published figure found.

benchmarks.value: clean, visual and meter NDT, hydro-test, band, paint
benchmarks.population: An oilfield service company's in-house iron recertification department

pain_points.description: Iron moves only when fleets move, so due pieces come home late and certified spares must be kept to cover the swap.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of common practice.

pain_points.description: The iron register is a spreadsheet keyed by serial number; mistyped serials and missing bands lead to expired iron on location or arguments at customer audits.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of common practice.

pain_points.description: Worn or mismatched hammer unions and eroded iron cause line failures that are a leading struck-by hazard on frac sites, so inspection quality matters more than speed.

evidence.note: Worn or mismatched hammer unions and line failures as hazards (src4).

sources.title: Trican Well Service Ltd. Management's Discussion and Analysis for the year ended December 31, 2022
sources.supports: Stainless steel fluid end costs of $7.5 million in 2022 and $8.0 million in 2021 ($1.2 million in Q4 2022) as the item that drives variability in repair and maintenance expense; higher active equipment raised repair and maintenance costs; personnel costs include operational support personnel such as mechanics; long lead times on key parts and record inflation in 2022; maintenance capital $29.96 million in 2022 and $23.5 million in 2021; fluid ends pump abrasive slurry at up to 15,000 psi and are modular units replaced independently of the power end; spring break-up road weight limits reduce oilfield activity; seven active and five parked frac crews in 2022.

sources.title: 903 Well Site Completion and Servicing Safety, module 2: hydraulic fracturing hazards
sources.supports: Struck-by hazards from high-pressure lines; mismatched or excessively worn hammer unions and line failures as causes; controls include inspecting hammer unions for excessive wear, fastening lines together, keeping non-essential personnel clear; pressure tests are taken above the maximum fracturing pressure but below the lowest component failure pressure.

sources.title: Road bans
sources.supports: Road bans reduce maximum weights on roads during weak or thawing conditions; spring heavy haul weights start when thaw depth reaches 25 cm; provincial highway and municipal bans; exemptions by permit from the Central Permit Office.

sources.title: Recertification - 100% Quality
sources.supports: High-pressure iron recertification steps used by a service company's in-house department: clean and prep the iron, visually inspect for defects and test it non-destructively with meters, hydro-test, band and paint; the same process for every piece.

assumptions: One case is one piece of iron (a straight joint, swivel, valve, tee or cross) taken from the due list to certified or condemned; pieces travel and are tested in batches, so waits are batch waits.

A yearly certificate with ultrasonic thickness readings and a hydrostatic test, and magnetic particle inspection on a longer cycle (about one piece in four each year), is the common practice assumed; no published WCSB interval was found, so intervals and test pressures are tier C.

The organisation file lists only pump technicians and heavy-duty mechanics on this process. Yard operators (washing, unloading), the planner (register and swaps) and the shop manager (sign-off) also take part, and many shops staff a dedicated iron shop crew with less experienced helpers, a role the organisation file lacks.
Iron comes home from frac fleets with rig-down and moves, so this file adds fo-frac-rig-down-and-move as a trigger beside the PM due list.
The test bay is added as a resource (3 bays) because the organisation file has none for pressure testing.
Staffing: about 7.6 FTE in all (4 of them pump technicians, a sixth of the 25 in the organisation file), close to the hands-on time times 600 pieces a month at 130 productive hours.
Loaded costs are the organisation file's (wage x 1.35).
